title: CoolDrip, first version
subtitle: An upright ice-drip coffee machine with a phone and watch app
context: Final-year project at SIVA DeTao School of Design, Shanghai. The first version of what became my 2024 graduation project.
role: Industrial designer: research, interviews, sketches, product design, app UI, coffee packaging, physical model
summary: This is the first version of CoolDrip from 2023, an upright ice-drip coffee machine with a removable water tank, an internal cooling fan and an electronic valve, paired with a phone and watch app. Earlier than the hourglass maker, this project began while I was studying how different coffee machines are built and making my first exploration into low-temperature coffee extraction.

sections.heading: First look at cold extraction
sections.body:
The later hourglass CoolDrip grew directly out of this piece, though the work here was more exploratory and structural. I was studying how different coffee machines are put together and testing viable ways to extract coffee at low temperature before the later form took shape.

The background research looked at how coffee had become a tool for staying awake. Caffeine peaks 30 to 60 minutes after a cup and carries a half-life of up to five hours, so cups through the day accumulate. Four coffee drinkers I interviewed captured the strain of wanting the flavour without the reliance. One said, "I love feeling the flavor of coffee, but I don't want to rely on it as much as I do now." Comparing five types of coffee maker pointed toward ice drip, which is slow and involved, with lower caffeine, a distinct flavour and drops falling like sand in an hourglass.

sections.heading: Working out the upright machine
sections.body:
Studying machine architecture led to an upright layout that can run through the app or be set directly with a physical knob, like winding a mechanical timer. Because ice needs storage and cleaning access, the upper water tank lifts off.

Inside the body, a mid-mounted fan exhausts inward to stay quiet alongside electronic temperature control, while an electronic valve controls flow rate because faster flow lowers extraction. A water mesh spreads drops evenly over the filter paper, and the extractor head lowers during brewing so an unfinished brew is clear at a glance. The material callouts pair glossy plastic, matte plastic and matte metal.

sections.heading: App, filter box and model
sections.body:
Around the machine, the phone app asks how many cups a person drinks each day, plots estimated caffeine in the body as a curve, pairs it with an "I'm sleepy" button, and folds coffee breaks into a daily to-do list. On the watch, chosen from three layout studies, the wearer can record sleepiness, view exercise data and take breaks paced by vibration. I also designed a coffee box that doubles as the filter, using a water filter cloth for uniform drip speed and a bean-and-leaf logo around de-instrumentalising coffee.

To test the structure at full scale, I 3D printed the parts, then ground, bonded, filled, primed, spray painted and sealed them with glossy and matte clear coats. Standing that upright model on a real counter gave me the groundwork that led into the hourglass CoolDrip the following year.
